refnamediv.refpurpose: Gets line from stream resource up to a given delimiter

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.description;
stringfalsestream_get_line resourcestream intlength stringending""
Gets a line from the given handle.
Reading ends when length bytes have been read, when the non-empty string specified by ending is found (which is not included in the return value), or on EOF (whichever comes first).
Unlike fgets, which keeps the delimiter and returns at most length - 1 bytes, this function reads up to length bytes, accepts any delimiter and does not return the delimiter itself.

&reftitle.parameters;
stream
A valid file handle.
length
The maximum number of bytes to read from the handle. Negative values are not supported. Zero (0) means the default socket chunk size, i.e. 8192 bytes.
The delimiter is only searched for within the first length bytes, so it has to lie entirely inside them: a delimiter that is cut by the limit is returned partly as data, and a delimiter longer than length is never found. An empty string can be returned, so compare the result with &false; strictly rather than testing it for truthiness.
ending
An optional string delimiter. If empty (the default), no delimiter is used and reading stops only after length bytes or at the end of the stream.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
Returns a string of up to length bytes read from the file pointed to by stream,&return.falseforfailure;. &false; is also returned at the end of the stream when nothing is left to read, and, on a non-blocking or timed-out stream, when no complete record is available yet: the data read so far stays buffered and is returned by a later call.

&reftitle.errors;
Throws a ValueError if length is negative.
